active.name: Follower
active.note: Copies the [set | position | _] template, takes the pointer’s [across | away] off the nest, puts it in the empty hole, and gives the message to the bird on the perch. Nothing in it is about pointers: it dozes until a reading arrives.

thing.text:
FOLLOWING

The pointer device delivers
[across | away].

A thing's bird takes
[set | position | [x | z]].

The box the device gives is
exactly the box the message
wants, so the robot only has
to put one inside the other.

TO RUN IT

Press SPACE on the star, then
move the pointer over the
table: it follows your hand.
"." stops it.

THE ROBOT IS ON ITS BACK.
Hold the star and press
Ctrl+P (or the gear on the
holding card) to go through
its door and watch the
robot at work. Escape
comes back out.

It dozes between moves: with
nothing on the pointer nest
there is nothing to match.

THE TEST OF A DESIGN

Nothing in these four steps
is about pointers, and
nothing is about position.
The robot copies a box, moves
a thing into a hole, and
gives it to the bird on the
perch -- three gestures it
could already do.

The device and the message
were designed a week apart
and fit because both are
DATA and neither is a
feature.
